# tmtv — Your terminal. Better together.

Open-source terminal sharing over SSH and an optional browser viewer. Pair,
troubleshoot and teach in a shared terminal. Host platforms: Linux and macOS.
License: ISC. Author: Lars-Erik Jonsson.

Current published stable release: 2.0.4.
Upcoming release: 3.0.0, in preparation, based on pinned tmux 3.8 sources and
sharing protocol 11. Upcoming does not mean published or deployed.

## Documentation

- Website: https://tmtv.se/
- Source and usage: https://github.com/sa3lej/tmtv
- Release log: https://tmtv.se/releases/
- 3.0 preview and coordinated upgrade guide: https://tmtv.se/releases/3-0/
- Published releases: https://github.com/sa3lej/tmtv/releases
- Snapshot limits: https://github.com/sa3lej/tmtv/blob/develop/docs/snapshot-protocol.md

## Install and join

Install the published release: curl -fsSL https://tmtv.se/install.sh | sh
macOS Homebrew: brew install sa3lej/tap/tmtv
Run tmtv to start a host. SSH guests use: ssh TOKEN@tmtv.se
Ordinary SSH guests do not need tmtv installed.

Web sharing is opt-in: tmtv set -g tmtv-web-sharing on
Browser input is a separate opt-in: tmtv set -g tmtv-web-input on
The host supplies a browser link at https://tmtv.se/s/TOKEN when web sharing is enabled.

## Capabilities and boundaries

Separate read-only and read-write invitations. Read-only guests cannot type and
do not receive shared clipboard access. Web input additionally requires the host's
input setting. Optional session passwords and self-hosted relays are supported.
Treat access tokens as credentials. Named public URLs are not secret access controls.
The relay processes terminal data; SSH transport encryption is not end-to-end
host-to-guest encryption through an untrusted relay.

The same running host can automatically reconnect and retain its identity and links.
Full host restarts create fresh credentials. Session names are availability-based;
name collisions during a gap can change links. Recording uses asciinema cast format.

3.0 adds a tmux 3.8 core, richer bounded layout/snapshot transfers and portable
Unicode sharing input. Supported reconnect state includes text attributes, OSC 8
hyperlinks and SIXEL images. Documented size/history and state limitations apply.
Unsupported live sharing layouts end sharing explicitly; local operation can continue.

## 3.0 upgrade

Protocol 11 is incompatible with 2.x and earlier develop protocol versions. Upgrade
hosts and relays together with matching web assets. Wait for the public service's
announced cutover before switching a host that uses it. Replacing the executable
does not upgrade an already running host. Save work before restarting: this ends
the local tmux server and may terminate pane programs. Restarted hosts need new links.
Publication and production deployment are separate operations.
